Self-hosted

Run AgentRaaS on your own servers

For production, self-host: your API keys and your agents' data never leave your infrastructure. It is free with no action limit and no license key, Team features (human approvals, SSO) included. Only Enterprise features need a key you add to the same install.

git clone https://github.com/sumedhchatse/agentraas
cd agentraas
./install.sh

install.sh generates fresh secrets, runs the database migrations and starts the stack (Postgres, Redis, the API and dashboard). The first run compiles from source and takes a few minutes. Kubernetes: see the Helm chart.

PlatformYou needRun it from
LinuxDocker with Compose, or Podman with podman-composeAny terminal
macOSDocker Desktop (Apple silicon or Intel), runningTerminal
WindowsWSL2 (wsl --install) and Docker Desktop with WSL integration onA WSL (Ubuntu) terminal. Clone inside WSL, not on C:\, or Postgres can't set its file permissions.

Editions

EditionPriceWhat you get
CommunityFree, AGPL-3.0Exactly-once execution, MCP gateway, dashboard, audit trail, circuit breaker, dead-letter queue, undo log, record and replay, spend caps and action policies that block, PII/DLP redaction. Unlimited actions.
TeamFree, no keyEverything in Community, plus human approvals (Slack, Teams, Telegram, Discord or email), approval holds on spend caps and policies, semantic dedup, OIDC SSO, up to 3 seats.
EnterpriseTalk to usEverything in Team, plus agent identity, inbound webhook receivers, white-label branding per client tenant, unlimited seats.

Self-hosted AgentRaaS has no action limit. Without a license key the server runs with Community and Team features and always starts; a missing or expired key falls back to that.

Adding a license key

  • Only Enterprise features need a key. Email hello@agentraas.io for one.
  • Put it in .env as LICENSE_TOKEN and restart the API container.
  • The key is checked on your server; nothing phones home.

Before production

  • Set PUBLIC_URL to your real domain: approval links, email links and the Connect Agent URLs use it.
  • Behind a reverse proxy, set CLIENT_IP_HEADER so rate limits apply per visitor.
  • Set SMTP_* for password resets and email alerts.
  • Back up Postgres: it holds the audit trail and stored credentials (encrypted with CREDENTIALS_ENCRYPTION_KEY; keep that key safe).

All settings: Self-hosting in the docs.
